title: Keep it. Find it. Reopen it.
assignment: Take one piece of your existing work and prove you can leave it, return to it, and keep an experiment separate from the original.
why: A sound is only reusable when you can find and reopen it. This exercise turns saving from a hopeful button press into something you can demonstrate.
setup: Begin after the current setup audit, with a project you recognize. Establish a verified save route before making edits. Do not rename files in the browser, delete duplicate candidates, format media, or close unsaved work. Use a clearly named working copy, not your only original.

steps.title: Recognize the original
steps.text: Listen to a short familiar part. Note the project name and two identifying features—for example a particular sound and one event or phrase. These become your return test.

steps.title: Preserve before exploring
steps.text: Use the project's Save As operation to save a distinct practice copy in a known writable location. Confirm the actual name and storage device on the save screen. If Save As or the location is unclear, stop and verify the screen instead of guessing.

steps.title: Make a reversible fingerprint
steps.text: Only in the saved practice copy, reduce one track's level by a small audible amount. Write down the original value. Save the practice copy again. Do not alter the sample file itself.

steps.title: Return and compare
steps.text: Once saving is confirmed, reopen the original and listen for its identifying features. Then reopen the practice copy. Does only the copy have the quieter part? A load error or missing sound is a result to investigate, not proof that the original was lost.

steps.title: Use what you kept
steps.text: Return to the practice copy and play with it. At your next session, try finding that copy without these instructions. Decide whether the naming and location actually helped.

listenFor: Do the expected sounds and recorded parts return?
Is the original distinct from the practice copy?
Can you locate the copy without opening several guesses?
concept: The project file and its associated sound/data files are not interchangeable. Moving or renaming one without the other can break loading. A second copy on the same storage device is useful for experiments but is not an independent backup.
hints: Identify the project-saving menu and its Save As choice on your installed MPC version before editing. Record that exact route and actual location in your journal; this brief does not invent a universal shortcut.
A suggested new name is 'Practice — <existing project name>'. This is a proposed name, not a claim that such a file already exists. Preserve the original and its associated data.
check: I have identified the actual original and practice-copy names and locations.
Both reopen with their expected material.
I can explain what is a working copy and what still needs an independent backup.
recovery: If there is any uncertainty about saving, do not close the current project or overwrite the original. Record the message and storage location. Never solve a missing-file error by deleting unexplained folders.
keep: The exact original/copy paths, the two identifying features, and the actual reopen result. Unknown fields stay unknown. Do not upload the music just to prove that it exists.
